In this study, a total of 225 participants were needed as there were 45 parameters (25 variable-to-variable paths, 10 standard error paths to the model variables, five BMI-to-variable paths, and five BMI standard error paths) in Fig. 1. Our sample size also exceeded the N 
 200 recommendation for complex models (Weston & Gore, 2006).

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the test of a hypothesized model, starting with the justification of the sample size (N = 249) and the statistical methods used (Mplus, CFI, SRMR, RMSEA). It describes the examination of an initial structural model, the subsequent trimming of nonsignificant paths, and a final revision based on modification indices to achieve a more parsimonious and better-fitting model. The final model's significant standardized path coefficients are presented in Fig. 2, with body appreciation variance notably accounted for by several factors.
